title.en: COVID-19 Resilience Certificate and Medal Rules 2022

completenessNote: 全文，共 12 条；逐字取自新加坡法规在线（SSO）官方打印视图，未改写、未节选。附表 1 篇以 900000+ 序号随同收录。

text.en: 1. These Rules are the COVID-19 Resilience Certificate and Medal Rules 2022.

3.—(1) The Certificate is designated and styled the COVID‑19 Resilience Certificate.
(2) The Medal is designated and styled the COVID-19 Resilience Medal.

heading.en: Awarding authority for Certificate and Medal

text.en: 4. The Minister may award the Certificate and the Medal.

5.—(1) The Certificate may be awarded to a group of individuals who collectively contributed to Singapore’s fight against the COVID‑19 pandemic.
(2) The Medal may be awarded to an individual who directly participated in Singapore’s fight against the COVID-19 pandemic.
(3) The Medal may be awarded to an individual even if the individual is a member of a group that has been awarded the Certificate.
(4) The Medal may be awarded posthumously.

6. A Certificate must bear —
(a)the words “COVID-19 Resilience Certificate”;
(b)the name or a description of the group that is awarded the certificate; and
(c)the signature of the Minister awarding the Certificate.

7.—(1) The Medal consists of a silver disc embellished along its rim with 8 arrows pointing inward.
(2) The obverse side of the Medal bears a crescent and 5 stars, encircled by the words “COVID-19” and “RESILIENCE MEDAL”.
(3) The reverse side of the Medal bears the State Crest, encircled by the words “SG UNITED” and “STRONGER TOGETHER”.
(4) The Medal has the design set out in the Schedule.

8.—(1) The Medal is to be worn on the left side of the recipient’s outer garment suspended by a ribbon.
(2) The ribbon has a red stripe at its centre, flanked on each side by a white stripe, a light turquoise stripe, and a dark turquoise stripe, in that order.

heading.en: Publication of Certificate and Medal recipients

text.en:
9.—(1) The name or a description of a group who has been awarded the Certificate must be published in the Gazette.
(2) The name of an individual who has been awarded the Medal must be published in the Gazette.
(3) However, if a group and an individual have been awarded the Certificate and the Medal respectively for similar contributions, it is sufficient to publish the name or a description of the group in the Gazette.

10.—(1) The Minister may forfeit a Certificate awarded to a group if the Minister considers that the group should not have been awarded the Certificate.
(2) The Minister may forfeit a Medal awarded to an individual if —
(a)the individual is convicted by a court in Singapore of any criminal offence;
(b)the individual is guilty of misconduct or disloyalty to Singapore;
(c)the individual, being a public officer, is dismissed from the public service; or
(d)the Minister considers that the individual should not have been awarded the Medal.
(3) The Minister may restore a forfeited Certificate or Medal.

11.—(1) If a Certificate or Medal is lost, damaged or destroyed, the recipient may make a written report to the Minister.
(2) If the Minister is satisfied that the circumstances justify the replacement of the Certificate or Medal (as the case may be), the Minister may approve the replacement at the recipient’s expense.
(3) The functions of the Minister in this rule may be exercised by a Permanent Secretary.
